items.text: Explain the difference between data, information, and metadata with a real-world example
Classify any given data as structured, semi-structured, or unstructured and justify why
Explain what a DBMS is and why applications need it instead of accessing files directly
Describe the key differences between relational (SQL) and non-relational (NoSQL) databases
Name all four SQL command categories (DDL, DML, DCL, TCL) and give one command for each
Explain what an index does and describe its trade-off between reads and writes
Explain what AWS RDS is and list the six supported database engines
Describe how to connect a client tool to RDS using the endpoint URL and port number
Explain the difference between RDS Multi-AZ (high availability) and Read Replicas (read scaling)
Describe Amazon Aurora's key advantages: 6 copies across 3 AZs, 15 read replicas, 128 TB storage, faster failover
Explain what Amazon Redshift is and when to use it instead of RDS (OLAP vs OLTP)
Compare ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached — features, persistence, and use cases
Describe how ElastiCache solves the sticky sessions problem in multi-EC2 architectures
Explain what DynamoDB is and give two use cases where it's better than RDS
Identify the correct AWS database service given a use case scenario in an exam question
Correctly distinguish Multi-AZ (synchronous, idle standby, HA) vs Read Replicas (asynchronous, active, scaling)
State Aurora's exact specs: 5x MySQL speed, 6 copies, 3 AZs, 128 TB, 15 read replicas
Know default ports: MySQL=3306, PostgreSQL=5432, Redis=6379, Memcached=11211
Explain cache hit vs cache miss and what happens in each case
